newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to face shortage of cheaper gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Poland to face shortage of cheaper gasoline.

text.p: Poland is about to face shortages of the popular cheap 94-octane leaded gasoline, just days after it stabilised diesel fuel supply through sales from state reserves, the biggest distributor, CPN, said on Thursday.

"I estimate between 30 and 40 percent of our stations will have this kind of petrol, while the rest will have only other kinds," said Stefan Olczyk, sales director of state-owned CPN which controls nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,700 stations.

The shortage will be yet another sign of instability on Poland's fuels market, caused by high world oil prices coupled with domestic caps on prices of Polish-made liquid fuels which makes it unattractive for domestic refiners to produce.

Olczyk said the shortage would arise because the large Plock refinery had curbed sales and it was not profitable to import the 94-octane leaded gasoline, which remains popular because of the large number of old cars running on the cheaper fuel.
He said the more expensive fuels, 98-octane leaded and all unleaded gasoline, would be available to meet demand.

He added that diesel fuel, which had been unavailable in some regions over the last few weeks, was now in steady supply after CPN's additional purchases from state reserves and following imports, but its price was higher in some regions.
Prices are higher in those areas where fuels come from imports as current regulations set no limits on prices of imported fuels.

The government is delaying plans to liberalise prices -- which would make fuel production more profitable for domestic refineries -- to achieve its goal of cutting year-on-year inflation to 17 percent in December from 21.6 percent last year.
